text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian Postal Service to lay off 3,000 workers in the first batch of retrenchment expect to start this week.
- Aircraft and ships used for drug trafficking to or from Nigeria will be impounded, the chairman of the national drug agency has said.
- Central bank governor urges banks to continue lending to high priority sectors of the economy despite the abolition of mandatory credit allocations.
- A total of 2.5 billion naira has so far been spent on setting up the Calabar Export Processing Zone in eastern Nigeria.

- An acute cash shortage has forced Nigeria's six multinational oil production joint-venture partners to borrow from local banks in order to pay staff salaries and debts with local contractors. Sources said the amount borrowed has reached 20 billion naira. Oil companies are still waiting for government approval of this year's operating budget.
- Shell may spend eight billion naira developing a new oil well in Bayelsa state.
- Banks are undercutting each other in a war to lend money to perceived safe borrowers.
